scholarshipName: Erasmus+ International Credit Mobility (KA171) - student mobility for studies
provider: European Commission / national agencies, implemented by individual European HEIs
whoCanApply: Students already ENROLLED at a Tunisian higher education institution that holds a signed KA171 inter-institutional agreement with a specific European HEI. Tunisia is an eligible Partner Country (Region 3, Southern Neighbourhood). Not open to individual applicants - you cannot apply as a private person and you cannot use it to enrol in a European degree.
tunisianEligible: Yes as a Partner Country, BUT ONLY as an outgoing exchange student of a Tunisian university that has an agreement. Not usable by this candidate for a full master's.
subjectScope: Open: handbook states 'Student and staff mobility can take place in any subject area or academic discipline.' Music production would qualify if the agreement covers it.
coverage: Individual support paid at the rate of the DESTINATION country: EUR 900/month for Austria, Belgium, Denmark, Finland, France, Germany, Iceland, Ireland, Italy, Liechtenstein, Luxembourg, Netherlands, Norway, Sweden; EUR 850/month for Cyprus, Czechia, Estonia, Greece, Latvia, Malta, Portugal, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain; EUR 800/month for Bulgaria, Croatia, North Macedonia, Hungary, Lithuania, Poland, Romania, Serbia, Turkiye. Travel support by distance band: EUR 309 (500-1999 km, non-green) or EUR 417 green; EUR 395 (2000-2999 km) or EUR 535 green. Organisational support of EUR 500 per participant covers visa/insurance/linguistic preparation but is paid to the institutions, not the student.
duration: Physical mobility period can last from 60 days to 12 months (5-30 days for short-term doctoral or blended). MAXIMUM 12 MONTHS - structurally cannot cover a full 2-year master's.
numberOfAwards: Set per bilateral project; typically 2-10 students per agreement per year
deadline: Institution-level internal calls, usually Feb-April for the following academic year. The KA171 call for institutions closes annually in February.
howToApply: Through the international relations office of the Tunisian home university, not directly to the European host or to the Commission.
requiresAdmissionFirst: No - but requires current enrolment at a Tunisian HEI with an existing agreement, which is a harder bar for this candidate
competitiveness: Moderate within a given agreement, but access is gated by whether his Tunisian home institution has an agreement at all
notes: VERDICT ON THE QUESTION ASKED: Erasmus+ ICM CANNOT fund a full master's degree for a Tunisian. The handbook caps the physical mobility period at 12 months and the scheme is defined as credit mobility - a limited period of study abroad within ongoing studies at the home institution, after which the student returns home and the credits are recognised there. It therefore DOES NOT BELONG in this funding file as a route to a September 2027 master's. The full-degree Erasmus+ instrument for a Tunisian is Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters (already settled: DIGICREA, ReSound, WAVES). Additionally, this candidate is graduating now, so by Sept 2027 he would no longer be enrolled at a Tunisian HEI and would be ineligible even for the exchange version.

tunisianEligible: NO. The criterion 'Be a UK passport holder' is absolute and he does not hold one. He would meet the under-represented-background and financial-need criteria and would be inside the 18-25 age band, but the passport condition is dispositive.
ageLimit: 18-25 - note he will be roughly 24-26 at entry, so even the age band is marginal by 2027
subjectScope: YES on subject - Advanced Diploma in Music Production and Sound Engineering - but this is a DIPLOMA, not a master's, so it would not meet his stated goal even if he were eligible
coverage: Full course fees plus a contribution towards living expenses, plus an optional one-year work placement at Abbey Road Studios on completion
deadline: PRIOR CYCLE: Friday 13 March 2026, outcomes by end of April 2026, course start 25 May 2026. Expected 2027 window: roughly March 2027 - but irrelevant given the passport bar.
howToApply: Application to Abbey Road Institute London plus scholarship form
requiresAdmissionFirst: Must meet Advanced Diploma entry requirements and submit a completed course application
competitiveness: Very high - 2 awards
notes: Recorded as an explicit negative because Abbey Road is the most-cited name in this space and would otherwise be re-derived. Other Abbey Road Institute campuses (Amsterdam, Berlin, Miami, Mumbai) run separate local scholarships (e.g. the Pensado's Place Scholarship at Miami, the Sontronics Scholarship) with their own criteria - UNVERIFIED for Tunisian eligibility, and all are diploma-level rather than master's-level, so they do not serve his September 2027 master's goal.

scholarshipName: SSL for Students scholarship - NEGATIVE/LIMITED FINDING
provider: Solid State Logic (in partnership with SAE Institute)
whoCanApply: Reported as covering undergraduate tuition fees for ONE UK-BASED student joining SAE, over the two-year accelerated degree.
tunisianEligible: NO on two grounds: UK-based requirement, and undergraduate level only.
subjectScope: Audio/music production at SAE - on subject but wrong level
coverage: Full undergraduate tuition for the two-year accelerated degree
deadline: PRIOR CYCLE: tied to the September 2025 SAE intake. UNVERIFIED for later cycles.
howToApply: Via SAE
competitiveness: Very high - single award
notes: MANUFACTURER CLUSTER VERDICT. A systematic search across Solid State Logic, Neve, Genelec, Sennheiser, Steinberg, Avid, iZotope, Waves, Universal Audio, Focusrite, Native Instruments, Ableton and Splice found NO open, master's-level, internationally-eligible scholarship run directly by any of these manufacturers. The pattern is consistent: manufacturers either (a) run student DISCOUNT and free/subsidised software programmes rather than scholarships (SSL for Students, Steinberg and Avid education pricing, Ableton and Native Instruments edu licences, Splice student plans), or (b) route their philanthropy through third parties - Genelec, L-Acoustics, Audio Precision and Dolby all fund NAMED AWARDS INSIDE THE AES EDUCATIONAL FOUNDATION rather than running their own schemes. PRACTICAL CONSEQUENCE: the single AESEF application is the correct and essentially the only way to reach manufacturer money as a Tunisian. Individual manufacturer programmes are UNVERIFIED at page level for Neve, Sennheiser, iZotope, Waves, Universal Audio, Focusrite and Splice - no scholarship page was found for any of them.

scholarshipName: Offre nationale des bourses pour des etudes de mastere et de doctorat a l'etranger (bourses d'etudes a l'etranger)
provider: Ministere de l'Enseignement Superieur et de la Recherche Scientifique, Tunisia - DGAEMUET, portal best.rnu.tn
country: Tunisia (funds study in Europe, Canada and other destinations)
whoCanApply: Tunisian students among the 'laureats' - top-ranked graduates - who wish to pursue master's and/or doctoral studies abroad. Described on the portal as for 'etudiants, parmi les laureats, qui souhaitent poursuivre leurs etudes de Mastere et/ou de Doctorat a l'etranger'.
tunisianEligible: YES - this is the Tunisian government's own scheme and is by definition for Tunisian nationals. It is the single most important item in this file and was not previously covered.
ageLimit: UNVERIFIED - not stated on the public portal; the annual circulaire may impose one
subjectScope: UNVERIFIED AND CRITICAL. No field restriction is stated on the public portal and the homepage announcements are 'general in scope without field-specific restrictions noted', but the scheme is administered through a system that leans heavily towards science, engineering and agriculture (it is relayed by IRESA, the agricultural research and higher education institution, among others). WHETHER A MUSIC PRODUCTION / STUDIO CRAFT MASTER'S IS AN ACCEPTED FIELD MUST BE CONFIRMED FROM THE CIRCULAIRE 2027-2028 PDF. This is the single most consequential unknown in the whole file.
coverage: THE MOST COMPLETE PACKAGE FOUND FOR A TUNISIAN. For EU destinations: EUR 800 per month, structured as EUR 600 grant plus EUR 200 as a loan repayable over 10 years. For Canada: CAD 1,000 per month (CAD 800 grant + CAD 200 repayable loan over 10 years). PLUS tuition fees, social security, compulsory health insurance, study permits and transport costs.
duration: Duration of the master's (UNVERIFIED whether 1 or 2 years is the cap)
numberOfAwards: UNVERIFIED - the portal reports 3,638 scholarship/loan applications in 2025 and 1,870 partner universities abroad, but does not publish an award count
deadline: PRIOR CYCLE: results for the 2026-2027 academic year were announced on 30 January, which implies an application window in roughly October-December of the preceding year. EXPECTED 2027-2028 WINDOW: circulaire published around October 2026, applications closing approximately November-December 2026, results around January 2027. The 2026-2027 circulaire was posted on 24 October 2025. EXACT DEADLINE UNVERIFIED - the circulaire is a downloadable PDF that could not be retrieved.
applicationOpens: Approximately October, with the annual 'Circulaire' and country annexes
howToApply: Register and apply through the ministry portal at https://best.rnu.tn/dgaemuet/ , following the Circulaire and the destination-country annexes
requiresAdmissionFirst: UNVERIFIED - but almost certainly YES in practice, since the scheme pays tuition to a named foreign institution and the portal maintains a list of 1,870 recognised partner universities abroad. IF SO, THIS DRIVES HIS ENTIRE TIMELINE: he would need European admission decisions in hand by roughly November-December 2026 for a September 2027 start, which is far earlier than most European art-school admission cycles conclude. TREAT AS THE BINDING CONSTRAINT ON HIS CALENDAR UNTIL DISPROVED.
requiresWorkExperience: No - it is explicitly aimed at recent laureates, which suits a candidate graduating now
languageRequirement: Set by the destination institution; French-language destinations suit him best
competitiveness: High - awarded to 'laureats', i.e. it is merit-ranked on undergraduate results
notes: HIGHEST-PRIORITY ACTION ITEM IN THIS ENTIRE SWEEP. It is the only scheme found that would pay tuition, a monthly allowance, health insurance and travel for a Tunisian doing a master's in Europe, and it is his own government's, so nationality is not a barrier for once. Two things must be checked IMMEDIATELY, not in 2027: (1) whether arts/music/AFAM-type programmes are within the eligible fields, and (2) whether a prior admission letter is required at application, because that would pull his whole application calendar forward by six to nine months. The 2026-2027 circulaire page: https://best.rnu.tn/offre-nationale-des-bourses-pour-des-etudes-de-mastere-et-de-doctorat-a-letranger-au-titre-de-lannee-universitaire-2026-2027/ . Note also that the ministry separately publicises bilateral offers - e.g. five master's and five doctoral scholarships in the UAE for 2026-2027 covering tuition, registration, accommodation and food, open to all specialisations EXCEPT medical fields - which shows the ministry does run non-STEM-restricted bilateral windows.
flags: TIMELINE-CRITICAL: application window likely Oct-Dec 2026, and prior admission may be required - this could force European applications to be submitted in autumn 2026

scholarshipName: IsDB Scholarship Programme - Master of Science track (M.Sc.)
country: Saudi-Arabia-based multilateral; funds study in member countries and abroad
whoCanApply: Citizens of IsDB member countries. Tunisia is an IsDB member country, so a Tunisian national passes the nationality test.
tunisianEligible: Yes on nationality. BUT SEE SUBJECT SCOPE - the subject bar is what closes this, not the nationality bar.
ageLimit: UNVERIFIED - the programme booklets impose age caps but the figure could not be confirmed from an official page
subjectScope: NO - THIS IS THE DISQUALIFIER. The M.Sc. track supports 'studies in science, engineering, technology'; the wider IsDB programmes focus on medicine, engineering, agriculture and related fields (dentistry, pharmacy, veterinary science, nursing, nutrition, computer science, forestry, fishery). Music production, studio craft, mixing, mastering and sound direction are not development-STEM fields and are extremely unlikely to be accepted. UNVERIFIED against the official 2026-2027 booklet, which could not be retrieved, but the published field framing is consistent across sources. NOTE THE IRONY: his BSc in Software Engineering WOULD fit IsDB's fields - the master's subject is what fails.
coverage: Fully funded: monthly stipend, tuition fees, medical/health cover and travel allowance
duration: Typically up to 2 years for the master's track
deadline: PRIOR CYCLE: 31 January 2026. EXPECTED 2027 CYCLE: approximately 31 January 2027 - which would fit a September 2027 start. No pre-September-2026 risk.
howToApply: Online at isdb.org/scholarships
competitiveness: High
notes: Worth one email to IsDB to test whether a music technology / audio engineering master's could be argued into the 'technology' bracket - his software-engineering background makes that argument more plausible than it would be for a conservatoire applicant, and the payoff (full funding) is large. But plan on the assumption that it is closed on subject. The IsDB M.Sc. track was originally created as a feeder for the Merit Scholarship Programme aimed at Least Developed Member Countries; Tunisia is not an LDMC, which may further restrict which track is open to him - UNVERIFIED. Official M.Sc. programme PDF: https://www.isdb.org/sites/default/files/media/documents/2024-02/Master%20of%20Science%20Scholarship%20Program%20(M.Sc_.)%20for%20IsDB%20Least%20Developed%20Member%20Countries%20f_0.pdf

scholarshipName: France Excellence Eiffel scholarship (master's level) - SUBJECT-SCOPE NEGATIVE
provider: Ministere de l'Europe et des Affaires etrangeres, administered by Campus France; relayed in Tunisia by the Institut francais de Tunisie
whoCanApply: International students nominated by a French higher education institution. Campus France states 'Only applications submitted by French higher education institutions are accepted' - the student cannot apply directly. Tunisians are eligible by nationality and Tunisia is an active Eiffel country (18 Tunisian laureates received Eiffel certificates in 2025/2026).
tunisianEligible: Yes by nationality - but see subject scope, which is what closes it.
ageLimit: Up to 29 years old at master's level. He would be 24-26 at entry, so he is comfortably inside.
subjectScope: NO - THIS IS THE DISQUALIFIER. The eligible fields at master's level are: biology and health; ecological transition; mathematics and digital; science and engineering; French history, language and civilisation; law and political science; economics and management. ARTS, MUSIC AND CREATIVE PRACTICE ARE NOT AMONG THE ELIGIBLE FIELDS. A music production or studio craft master's does not fall into any Eiffel discipline. (An audio-signal-processing or music-informatics master's inside an engineering school could arguably fall under 'mathematics and digital' or 'science and engineering' - that is the only way Eiffel becomes live for him, and it would mean choosing an engineering-framed programme rather than a conservatoire one.)
coverage: EUR 1,181 per month at master's level, plus an international return air ticket and social security cover. Does not pay tuition, but French public tuition is low.
duration: Up to 12 months for master's (up to 24 in some configurations - UNVERIFIED)
deadline: PRIOR CYCLE: 8 January 2026 for receipt of applications by Campus France (2026 session). EXPECTED 2027 CYCLE: approximately 8 January 2027 - and note the FRENCH INSTITUTION must assemble and submit the file well before that, so his contact with the institution has to start in autumn 2026.
applicationOpens: Autumn (institutions build files from roughly October)
howToApply: The French institution submits on his behalf to candidatures.eiffel@campusfrance.org - he must first secure the institution's willingness to nominate him
requiresAdmissionFirst: Effectively YES - the institution nominating him must have him as an applicant/admittee
languageRequirement: French for French-taught programmes - he is fluent, which is a genuine advantage here
competitiveness: Very high
notes: IMPORTANT STRATEGIC POINT. Eiffel is the largest French award a Tunisian can access and his French fluency and age both fit, but the discipline list excludes the arts. This is the SECOND scheme in his file (after DAAD's music award) where the subject rather than the nationality is the barrier - the pattern is that generalist excellence schemes fund STEM and social science, while arts funding sits in a separate, much smaller ecosystem. If he wanted Eiffel he would have to reframe his target towards an engineering-school audio/signal-processing master's (e.g. at Universite Gustave Eiffel or an ESAV/UBO-adjacent technical route). Also relevant from the same source: the Institut francais de Tunisie / French Embassy run a Master 2 Recherche excellence scholarship, created in 2013, financing M2 research mobility WITHIN a Franco-Tunisian inter-university partnership or double-degree agreement, with calls launched annually in MAY - that requires an existing partnership between his Tunisian institution and a French one, and is research-M2-shaped rather than professional-master-shaped. UNVERIFIED for arts eligibility.
flags: SUBJECT-SCOPE BAR: arts and music are not eligible Eiffel disciplines

scholarshipName: Prix Rambourg pour l'Art et la Culture (Fonds d'encouragement a la creation litteraire et artistique)

scholarshipName: British Council MENA / Goethe-Institut Tunis / Anna Lindh Foundation / Drosos Foundation - CLUSTER FINDING, NO INDIVIDUAL STUDY FUNDING
whoCanApply: These four operate as programme funders and cultural-relations bodies rather than scholarship providers for individuals. The Anna Lindh Foundation funds civil-society NETWORK organisations (in Tunisia the network head is We Love Sousse, appointed 2012) and issues calls for intercultural-dialogue PROJECTS, not personal study grants. Drosos Foundation funds partner ORGANISATIONS running youth and creative-skills projects and does not accept unsolicited individual applications. British Council MENA and Goethe-Institut Tunis run programmes, residencies, training and language provision; their scholarship activity is channelled into named schemes (GREAT, Chevening, DAAD) that are already established as closed to him.
tunisianEligible: Tunisia is within all four bodies' geographies, but NONE of them was found to run an open individual scholarship for master's study abroad.
subjectScope: Culture and creative practice generally
coverage: Project and organisational grants, not tuition or stipends
deadline: Rolling programme calls
howToApply: Through calls published by each body; Anna Lindh via alf.website/en/network/tunisia/
competitiveness: n/a
notes: UNVERIFIED at the level of an exhaustive page-by-page check of each organisation's current calls - the conclusion is that none of the four is structured as an individual study funder, which is a structural rather than a nationality finding. The practical use of Goethe-Institut Tunis and the Institut francais de Tunisie to him is LANGUAGE CERTIFICATION and networking, not money: a Goethe German certificate would be the only route to the German-language production masters (Popakademie requires C1 German), and the IFT hosts Campus France Tunisie, which is the mandatory channel for any French public-university application via the Etudes en France platform.
